query: A CVS pharmacist is counselling a patient who just started taking metformin for Type 2 diabetes. The patient is worried about side effects. What are the most commonly reported adverse events for metformin based on FDA reports?
A Signify Health home health aide is visiting an elderly patient aged 78 on lisinopril for hypertension. What does the FDA label say about use of lisinopril in geriatric patients?
A CVS pharmacist has a patient picking up extended-release metformin. Before dispensing, check for any active FDA recalls AND retrieve the key storage instructions from the official drug label.

A patient taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation is asking whether they can take ibuprofen for a headache. Check the drug label for warfarin regarding drug interactions AND look up adverse events for warfarin to understand the severity of bleeding risks.
A CVS store manager needs to check if any blood pressure medications containing valsartan are currently under active FDA recall.

A Medicare patient is picking up a new prescription for lisinopril 10mg from CVS. Perform a complete safety check: first check for active recalls, then retrieve the black box warning and contraindications from the drug label, and finally check what serious adverse events have been reported.

A Medicare patient cannot afford Jardiance (empagliflozin) and asks about a cheaper alternative for Type 2 diabetes. Check if there are recalls on Jardiance, then get the label to confirm its indications, then check adverse events for metformin as a cheaper alternative.

A customer at CVS MinuteClinic wants to take extra-strength Tylenol (acetaminophen 500mg) for pain. They mention they drink alcohol regularly. Check the drug label for acetaminophen warnings about alcohol AND look up adverse events to understand liver risk.
A patient who is newly pregnant tells a Signify Health nurse they are taking atorvastatin for high cholesterol. What does the FDA label say about use of atorvastatin during pregnancy?

A parent asks a CVS pharmacist if their 8-year-old child can take aspirin for fever, and whether there are any safety concerns. Check the drug label for aspirin paediatric use AND look up adverse events in paediatric patients.
Patient P001 is at the CVS pharmacy counter to pick up their prescriptions. Look up their patient record first, then check all their current medications for any active FDA recalls.

ground_truth.patient: P001 — John Smith, age 72, on warfarin and lisinopril

notes: Tests get_patient_record tool. Agent must retrieve P001 record first, then check recalls for each medication found (warfarin + lisinopril = 2 recall checks).
